title: Multi-site OSPF network with redundancy and FHRP
summary: Connect a headquarters and two branches with single-area OSPF, redundant links, an HSRP gateway pair and a floating static backup route, then prove failover works.
why: Redundancy and dynamic routing are what keep real networks running. Showing that you planned for failure, tested it and documented the results separates you from candidates who only passed the exam.
brief:
Build a company with a headquarters (HQ) and two branch sites in Packet Tracer or Cisco Modeling Labs. HQ has two routers and switches serving the user VLANs; each branch has one router and a LAN. Connect the sites with point-to-point links so that every branch has two paths to HQ (a triangle or partial mesh), and connect HQ to a simulated ISP.

Run single-area OSPFv2 (area 0) on all internal routers. Set router IDs by hand, use the point-to-point network type on WAN links, make user-facing interfaces passive, and advertise a default route into OSPF from the HQ edge with default-information originate. Tune interface costs so traffic prefers the path you choose, and show the path changing when that link fails. At HQ, run HSRP on the user VLANs so hosts keep their gateway if one HQ router dies, with preemption and tracking of the uplink. Add a floating static default route as a backup.

The heart of the project is the failover report. For each failure (a WAN link, an HQ router, the ISP link), record what you expected, what actually happened, how long recovery took (count the lost pings) and which show commands proved it.

milestones.title: Design
tasks: Draw the topology with sites, links, interfaces and link speeds
Plan addressing: /30 or /31 point-to-point links, loopbacks for router IDs and user subnets per site
Decide each site's primary and backup path and how you will make OSPF prefer it
milestones.doneWhen: A diagram and an addressing table exist, and the design doc names the intended primary and backup path for each site.

milestones.title: OSPF adjacencies
tasks: Configure OSPF with manual router IDs
Set the point-to-point network type on WAN links and make user LAN interfaces passive
milestones.doneWhen: `show ip ospf neighbor` shows every expected adjacency in the FULL state, and every router has a route to every subnet.

milestones.title: Default route and path control
tasks: Configure a default route to the ISP and default-information originate on the HQ edge router
Adjust interface costs or the reference bandwidth so the preferred path wins
Check the results with show ip route and traceroute
milestones.doneWhen: Branch routers learn an O*E2 default route, and traceroute from each branch follows the planned primary path.

milestones.title: Gateway redundancy with HSRP
tasks: Configure HSRP on each HQ user VLAN, with the virtual IP as the hosts' default gateway
Set priorities and preempt so the intended router is active
Track the uplink so the active router gives up its role when it loses its WAN path
milestones.doneWhen: `show standby brief` shows the planned active and standby router for every group.

milestones.title: Failover tests
tasks: Fail a WAN link, an HQ router and the ISP link one at a time while pinging continuously
Record the lost pings and the new path for each test
Add a floating static default route with an administrative distance above 110, then test it by removing the OSPF default
milestones.doneWhen: A failover table lists every test with expected and observed results, and traffic recovers in every case.

stretch: Add EtherChannel between the HQ switches and align the STP root bridge with the HSRP active router
Run OSPFv3 for IPv6 alongside OSPFv2
Add OSPF authentication on the WAN links
Rebuild it in Cisco Modeling Labs and record real convergence times
rubric: A reviewer should see a diagram and addressing plan that match the configs
A reviewer should see manual router IDs, passive user interfaces and point-to-point WAN network types
A reviewer should see a deliberate path preference set with costs and verified with traceroute
A reviewer should see HSRP with preemption and tracking, and hosts using the virtual gateway
A reviewer should see a failover table with expected and observed results for at least three failures
A reviewer should see a floating static route whose administrative distance is higher than OSPF's
A reviewer should see saved show command output backing each claim in the report
showcase: Create a GitHub repository with per-device configs, the topology diagram, the design doc and the failover report with show output
Put the topology diagram and the failover results table at the top of the README
Add a short 'What surprised me' section, for example how long HSRP or OSPF took to converge
Mention the failover testing explicitly on your resume; it is the part employers care about
resumeBullet: Built a 3-site network with single-area OSPF, HSRP gateway redundancy and a floating static backup route; tested 5 failure scenarios and documented recovery behavior with show-command evidence on GitHub.
interviewTalkingPoints: How OSPF picks a path, and how you made it prefer the link you wanted
Why passive interfaces and manual router IDs matter
What HSRP tracking adds, and what goes wrong without preemption
How a floating static route uses administrative distance to stay out of the way until it is needed
Which failure took longest to recover from, and why
